Evidence: Part 5 consumes the Part 1 capacity result rather than rebuilding the capacity calculation.
Applicability: All workloads for which Part 1 capacity analysis is applicable.
Limitations: Part 1 must have sufficient inputs; Part 5 does not repair missing capacity evidence.

Rule_Name: Capacity Failure Is a Hard Memory Constraint
Rule_Description: If Part 1 establishes that required applicable memory exceeds applicable available memory, classify a memory-capacity bottleneck and the overall memory configuration as not feasible.
Inputs: Part1_Capacity_Result
Condition: Part 1 reports FAIL / required applicable memory exceeds applicable available memory
Output_Decision: MEMORY_CAPACITY_BOTTLENECK; NOT FEASIBLE
Source_Title: Part 1 Memory Capacity
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 1 applicable-capacity feasibility comparison
Evidence: Part 1 defines failure when required applicable memory exceeds applicable available memory.
Applicability: Applicable memory capacity checks.
Limitations: A missing required-memory value is not failure; it is insufficient evidence.

Rule_Name: Unknown Capacity Demand Must Produce Insufficient Evidence
Rule_Description: If the required applicable memory is unknown or Part 1 cannot establish a capacity result, do not infer failure; return insufficient evidence for the capacity dimension.
Inputs: Part1_Capacity_Result; Required_Applicable_Memory
Condition: Required memory or required evidence is unknown
Output_Decision: CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
Source_Title: Part 1 Memory Capacity
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 1 capacity evidence-status logic
Evidence: Part 1 explicitly distinguishes unknown demand from failure.
Applicability: Cases with missing workload-specific memory demand.
Limitations: Unknown is neither pass nor fail.

Rule_Name: Training Result Must Be Inherited From Part 2
Rule_Description: For training/fine-tuning workloads, consume Part 2's component, placement, and per-device feasibility result rather than recalculating parameters, gradients, optimizer states, activations, or runtime memory.
Inputs: Part2_Training_Memory_Result; Per_Device_Training_Memory_Result; Placement_Result
Condition: Training/fine-tuning workload and Part 2 result is available
Output_Decision: INHERIT TRAINING MEMORY STATE
Source_Title: Part 2 Training Memory
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 2 training-memory decision outputs
Evidence: Part 5 consumes Part 2 outputs only for training/fine-tuning.
Applicability: Training and fine-tuning workloads.
Limitations: Training checks are not applicable to inference-only workloads.

Rule_Name: Training Placement Failure Produces Training Memory Bottleneck
Rule_Description: If Part 2 establishes that the training configuration cannot satisfy required per-device memory or required sharding/offload placement, classify a training-memory or placement bottleneck and overall infeasibility.
Inputs: Part2_Training_Memory_Result; Part2_Placement_Result
Condition: Required per-device memory or required placement cannot be satisfied
Output_Decision: TRAINING_MEMORY_BOTTLENECK; MEMORY_PLACEMENT_BOTTLENECK; NOT FEASIBLE
Source_Title: Part 2 Training Memory
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 2 per-device and placement feasibility
Evidence: Part 2 requires explicit placement/sharding evidence and per-device feasibility.
Applicability: Training configurations using replication, sharding, offload, or other placement.
Limitations: Do not use aggregate memory as a substitute for per-device placement evidence.

Rule_Name: Inference Result Must Be Inherited From Part 3
Rule_Description: For inference/serving workloads, consume Part 3's model, dynamic-memory, runtime, placement, and per-device feasibility results without recalculating them.
Inputs: Part3_Inference_Memory_Result; Part3_Per_Device_Result; Part3_Placement_Result
Condition: Inference/serving workload and Part 3 result is available
Output_Decision: INHERIT INFERENCE MEMORY STATE
Source_Title: Part 3 Inference Memory
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 3 inference-memory decision outputs
Evidence: Part 5 consumes Part 3 outputs for inference/serving.
Applicability: Online/interactive and batch/offline inference.
Limitations: Training-only KV-cache/runtime assumptions must not be applied to unrelated workloads.

Rule_Name: Inference Dynamic-Memory Failure Produces Inference Memory Bottleneck
Rule_Description: If Part 3 establishes that model weights plus applicable dynamic/runtime memory or placement cannot fit the selected inference configuration, classify an inference-memory or placement bottleneck and overall infeasibility.
Inputs: Part3_Inference_Memory_Result; Part3_Placement_Result
Condition: Applicable inference memory or placement result is FAIL
Output_Decision: INFERENCE_MEMORY_BOTTLENECK; MEMORY_PLACEMENT_BOTTLENECK; NOT FEASIBLE
Source_Title: Part 3 Inference Memory
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 3 inference-memory feasibility
Evidence: Part 3 explicitly requires weight, KV/runtime, per-device, and placement evidence.
Applicability: Inference/serving workloads.
Limitations: A model fitting by weights alone is insufficient when dynamic/runtime memory is required.

Rule_Name: Bandwidth Bottleneck Must Be Inherited From Evidence-Based Part 4 Analysis
Rule_Description: Classify memory bandwidth as a bottleneck only when Part 4 has sufficient measured, workload-derived, profiling, benchmark, or access-pattern evidence supporting a bandwidth limitation.
Inputs: Part4_Bandwidth_State; Measured_Bandwidth; Required_Bandwidth; Profiling_Evidence
Condition: Part 4 classifies bandwidth as a bottleneck using applicable evidence
Output_Decision: MEMORY_BANDWIDTH_BOTTLENECK
Source_Title: Part 4 Memory Bandwidth & Locality
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 4 bandwidth bottleneck evidence logic
Evidence: Part 4 explicitly rejects classification from workload size or theoretical bandwidth alone.
Applicability: Workloads with appropriate bandwidth measurements/evidence.
Limitations: No universal bandwidth utilization threshold is introduced.

Rule_Name: Locality Bottleneck Must Require Evidence of a Relevant Placement Constraint
Rule_Description: Classify memory locality/NUMA as a bottleneck only when Part 4 establishes that topology, affinity, remote-memory access, or accelerator locality materially constrains the workload.
Inputs: Part4_Locality_State; NUMA_Topology; Affinity_Evidence; Profiling_Evidence
Condition: Part 4 identifies an evidence-supported locality constraint
Output_Decision: MEMORY_LOCALITY_BOTTLENECK
Source_Title: Part 4 Memory Bandwidth & Locality
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 4 locality evidence logic
Evidence: Part 4 requires topology/locality evidence and prohibits universal NUMA penalties.
Applicability: NUMA, socket-locality, or accelerator-locality relevant configurations.
Limitations: Missing topology evidence is insufficient evidence, not a locality failure.

Rule_Name: Placement Failure Must Be Reported Independently of Aggregate Memory Capacity
Rule_Description: If the workload's required memory can exist in aggregate but cannot be placed on the required device/socket/NUMA domain according to Parts 2 or 3, classify a placement bottleneck.
Inputs: Per_Device_Result; Placement_Result; Aggregate_Memory; Topology
Condition: Aggregate capacity is available but required per-device/local placement is infeasible
Output_Decision: MEMORY_PLACEMENT_BOTTLENECK; NOT FEASIBLE
Source_Title: Parts 2 and 3 Memory Placement
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Per-device placement/sharding requirements
Evidence: Applies where training/inference placement requires per-device or topology-specific capacity.
Applicability: Aggregate memory is not treated as one shared pool.
Limitations: Requires applicable placement evidence.

Rule_Name: Only Applicable Memory Constraints Should Participate in the Final Decision
Rule_Description: Evaluate capacity, training/inference memory, bandwidth, locality, and placement only when each is applicable to the workload and configuration.
Inputs: Workload_Type; Applicability_Flags; Part1_Result; Part2_Result; Part3_Result; Part4_Result
Condition: Constraint is marked applicable
Output_Decision: INCLUDE CONSTRAINT IN FINAL MEMORY DECISION
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Part 5 applicability logic
Evidence: The specification explicitly says non-applicable training/inference/NUMA/bandwidth checks should not be required.
Applicability: All DSS workload modes.
Limitations: Applicability metadata must be determined correctly before final classification.

Rule_Name: Any Applicable Hard Memory Failure Makes the Configuration Not Feasible
Rule_Description: If at least one applicable hard memory constraint from Parts 1–4 fails, the final memory state is NOT FEASIBLE, while preserving all detected bottleneck labels.
Inputs: Applicable constraint states; Capacity; Training/Inference; Bandwidth; Locality; Placement
Condition: At least one applicable hard constraint is FAIL
Output_Decision: NOT FEASIBLE; RETAIN ALL APPLICABLE BOTTLENECKS
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Multi-constraint feasibility logic
Evidence: The specification defines feasibility as satisfaction of all applicable constraints.
Applicability: Any workload with one or more applicable hard memory constraints.
Limitations: Does not identify a single dominant bottleneck.

Rule_Name: All Applicable Memory Constraints Passing Produces FEASIBLE
Rule_Description: Return FEASIBLE only when every applicable memory constraint has sufficient evidence and passes.
Inputs: Applicable constraint states; Evidence_Status
Condition: Every applicable constraint is PASS and no required evidence is missing
Output_Decision: FEASIBLE
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Final three-state decision logic
Evidence: The specification defines FEASIBLE as all applicable memory constraints having sufficient evidence and passing.
Applicability: Any workload with complete applicable memory evidence.
Limitations: A non-applicable constraint must not be treated as a required pass.

Rule_Name: Missing Required Evidence Produces INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
Rule_Description: Return INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE when a required applicable input or evidence needed for a safe memory classification is missing and no hard failure has been established.
Inputs: Evidence_Status; Missing_Inputs; Part1_Result; Part2_Result; Part3_Result; Part4_Result
Condition: Required applicable evidence is missing and no applicable hard failure is established
Output_Decision: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Unknown/evidence-completeness logic
Evidence: The specification explicitly states that missing evidence is neither failure nor pass.
Applicability: Any workload with incomplete required evidence.
Limitations: If a hard failure is already established, NOT FEASIBLE takes precedence over missing secondary evidence.

Rule_Name: Multiple Memory Bottlenecks Must Be Preserved
Rule_Description: Allow capacity, training/inference, bandwidth, locality, and placement bottlenecks to coexist; do not collapse them into one winner without explicit evidence.
Inputs: All applicable bottleneck labels from Parts 1–4
Condition: Two or more applicable bottleneck conditions are simultaneously established
Output_Decision: RETAIN MULTIPLE MEMORY BOTTLENECKS
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Multiple-bottleneck requirement
Evidence: The specification explicitly allows multiple memory bottlenecks.
Applicability: Any workload where multiple hard or evidence-supported bottlenecks exist.
Limitations: No dominance ranking is created.

Rule_Name: Host, CPU-Attached, GPU, Sharded, and Offloaded Memory Must Remain Distinct
Rule_Description: Carry forward the placement identity of memory from Parts 1–4; do not merge host/system, CPU-attached, GPU, aggregate, sharded, or offloaded memory into one interchangeable capacity value.
Inputs: System_Memory_GB; GPU_Memory_Per_Accelerator_GB; GPU_Memory_Aggregate_GB; placement/sharding/offload state
Condition: A decision combines memory resources from different placement domains
Output_Decision: REQUIRE DOMAIN-CONSISTENT MEMORY EVIDENCE
Source_Title: Memory Capacity, Training Memory, Inference Memory
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Host/GPU/per-device/aggregate distinction
Evidence: The specification explicitly requires distinction among host, CPU-attached, GPU, per-device, aggregate, shared, sharded, and offloaded memory.
Applicability: All cross-catalogue memory decisions.
Limitations: Does not create new CPU/GPU/Server rules.

Rule_Name: Final Decision Must Preserve the Underlying Evidence Status
Rule_Description: Store the final state together with the applicable constraint results and evidence status so FEASIBLE, NOT FEASIBLE, or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE remains auditable.
Inputs: Final_Memory_State; Constraint_States; Evidence_Status; Bottleneck_Labels
Condition: Final decision is generated
Output_Decision: RETURN FINAL STATE WITH BOTTLENECKS, APPLICABILITY, AND EVIDENCE STATUS
Source_Title: Memory Parts 1–4 Integration
Exact_Page_Section_Table_Equation: Auditability of final decision state
Evidence: Supports DSS explainability and prevents loss of the evidence basis.
Applicability: All final memory decisions.
Limitations: This is an integration/output requirement, not a numerical scoring rule.
